title: Unable to use Streamlit behind HTTP proxy due to websocket errors
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit app is running inside a docker container behind a NGINX proxy under `/dashboard/` path.

The docker container is started as follows:
`
docker run -d -p 49500:8080 $DOCKER_IMAGE
`
Where `49500` is the external port, and `8080` is the internal NGINX port.
NGINX forward all requests to `http://ip:49500/dashboard/` to the Streamlit app running in the internal port `8081`.

The Streamlit app is started as follows:
`
streamlit run script.py --server.port=8081 --server.baseUrlPath="/dashboard/" --browser.gatherUsageStats=false --theme.base="light" --server.enableCORS=false --server.enableXsrfProtection=false &
`

Accessing the Streamlit app using the IP address works fine e.g. `http://ip:49500/dashboard/`.

However, while accessing the Streamlit app using a HTTP reverse proxy does not work e.g.
`https://<redacted-host>:8443/cloud-automation-service/services/6/endpoints/mlops-dashboard-gui-92-6/`.

Our HTTP reverse proxy forwards:
`https://<redacted-host>:8443/cloud-automation-service/services/6/endpoints/mlops-dashboard-gui-92-6/`
to:
`http://0.0.0.0:49500/dashboard/`

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

st.write("Hello, World!")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

The expected behavior is to be able to access the Streamlit app as follows

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/483114/224794291-cb83f7d2-75f0-40d9-932c-d2567b6cef4f.png)

The current behavior is

![Screenshot 2023-03-13 at 19 15 52](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/483114/224794468-40c5fc3b-1bd5-4622-840c-140b2ff016bb.png)


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.11.1
- Python version: 3.8.12
- Operating System: Debian GNU/Linux 11 (bullseye)
- Browser: Chrome, Firefox
- Virtual environment: Docker

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Could be related to this issue:
https://<redacted-host>/t/connection-error-failed-to-process-a-websocket-message/28776

Did you check if your reverse proxy strips the query parameters?
If the hash is not in the request, the streamlit server responds with a 404 which would fit your issue.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
We recently changed some internal URLs and also had a bug related to the message endpoint which got fixed here: 

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/6210

But if the app is still running `1.11.1` it might not be related to this issue. I would suggest updating to the latest version to see if you are running into the same issue. In general, it is very unlikely that we will investigate issues with older Streamlit versions.

comments.author: participant4
participant5
comments.body:
Regarding `location /stream` and `location ^~ /healthz`, they have changed place to `/_stcore/stream` and `_stcore/health` that's probably why `/stream` and `/healthz` were not working anymore, you may need to rename them in your nginx conf. Your `location /` is passing everything through so that works too.

Check out https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/5534/files for most of the endpoints renaming. There should be a public doc about it one day!

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
This is still an issue for us. The connection to the app from the client is established but it keeps loading for ever. Therefore, we cannot use Streamlit in our network.

All other libraries providing similar functionality we have tested so far work perfectly well. This includes Flask, Plotly Dash and Gradio.

The case of Gradio is interesting because, even though it does not strictly depend on WebSocket, we observe WebSocket traffic, which means that the protocol itself is not blocked.

For Flask and Dash we are still relying on the Werkzeug server, which does not depend on WebSocket, even though it seems to use it just for rerouting. Perhaps it is the same for Gradio.

comments.author: participant10
comments.body:
Works for me with streamlit 1.33.0 with Apache mod_proxy using this conf :

```
 <VirtualHost *:80>
        ServerName      *******
        ServerAdmin     <email-scrubbed>

        ErrorLog        ${APACHE_LOG_DIR}/error-streamlit.log
        CustomLog       ${APACHE_LOG_DIR}/access-streamlit.log combined
        ProxyPreserveHost       On
        ProxyRequests           Off
        <Proxy *>
                order deny,allow
                Allow from all
        </Proxy>
        ProxyPass        / "http://*****:8501/"
        ProxypassReverse / "http://*****:8501/"
        <Location "/_stcore/stream">
                ProxyPass               ws://*****:8501/_stcore/stream
                ProxyPassReverse        ws://*****:8501/_stcore/stream
        </Location>
</VirtualHost> 
```

Bumping as this worked for me as well. 

For anyone who might also need it, instead of proxypass, I was able to use a rewrite rule too:
```
        RewriteEngine on
        RewriteRule /_stcore/stream ws://0.0.0.0:$port/_stcore/stream [P,L]
```
